On Small Tools

Most of the tools I trust were written in an afternoon. They do one thing, and they do it the same way every time, which is the only kind of reliability I have ever been able to depend on.

A large tool asks you to learn its world before it lets you work. A small one asks for nothing but the file you were already holding. That difference compounds over years, because the small tool is still there when the large one has been replaced twice.

So when I start something new, I try to make the first version small enough to throw away. If it survives a month of use, it has earned a second afternoon.
